audit.why: HARD 8/10 matches WR 45.78 over 675 games and the kit read: untargetable E plus shark all-in against an immobile caster.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on every row: content win[] gives Taliyah 7/7 (packet flags this against the 45.78% WR) while full gives Fizz 7/7. Neither is credible end to end.
audit.why: Kit-grounded split: levels 1-5 Taliyah's 1000-range Q taxes a melee with no waveclear (Fizz Q dash is 550 range, E not up until 3 and 16s CD); from 6 Chum the Waters' attach-knockup plus untargetable E beats an immobile kit — which is what the diff 8/10, the tldr ('hug tower post-6') and the WR all say.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 -> Taliyah on both layers; rows 4-6 -> Fizz on both layers; every touched why rewritten to match its verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digits; the Seastone Trident auto-reset burst tell (missingInteractions) was absent; spikes[1].text claims 'you can W yourself out of the shark's path' — Taliyah's W displaces enemies, not herself.
audit.why: Kit: Playful/Trickster 16/14/12/10/8s, untargetable; Chum the Waters 120/100/80s, blockable projectile, knockup; Seastone Trident empowers his next attack (auto-reset tell); both his Q and E are dashes your E mines stun.
audit.corrected: Numbers and sequencing added; self-W claim removed in the spikes[1] rewrite; reset tell written into dontsFull[2].d.

edits.before: Fizz
edits.after: Taliyah

edits.before: Q on fresh ground shreds level-1 trades — most mids don't expect five stones at minute two. Manage your Worked Ground like mana.
edits.after: You win level 1 — Fizz is melee with no waveclear, so your 1000-range Q taxes every walk-up; his passive shaves the chip, not the trade.

edits.before: Fizz
edits.after: Taliyah

edits.before: W online: the shove-displacement already threatens kill angles against overstep-happy laners.
edits.after: Still yours at 2: shove him under tower — he pays health for every CS; his Q dash is only 550 range.

edits.before: Fizz
edits.after: Taliyah

edits.before: Full kit: W-into-E is the signature burst — shove him across the stones and watch half a health bar disappear.
edits.after: Level 3 he gets Playful/Trickster — bait the 16s hop before you commit, then W-E him on the landing frame.

edits.before: Fizz
edits.after: Taliyah

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-poke on every wave contact. Fresh-ground positioning is your real skill expression now.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you out-poke him if you bait E first — his hop dodges the whole combo, so spend nothing until it lands.

edits.before: Weaver's Wall online — you are now the best roaming mid in the game. Every shove is a bot-lane gank announcement.
edits.after: Level 6 is his: the shark's knockup into E-Q burst deletes you — hug tower, dodge the fish sideways, roam from safety.

edits.before: Luden's spike: the W-E-Q rotation deletes squishies. Force river fights where your stones pre-seed the geometry.
edits.after: Luden's helps the poke but one landed shark still flips it — shove from range and buy Zhonya's parts early.

edits.before: Late Taliyah edits maps: wall their reinforcements, shove their frontline into your team, and Q whatever stands on stones.
edits.after: Late he one-shots your carries off a single fish — group, wall his flank route, and keep W loaded to break the dive.

edits.before: Taliyah
edits.after: Fizz

edits.before: At 6 you stay ahead by shoving and dodging his Chum the Waters shark with W or wall.
edits.after: At 6 Fizz takes over: Chum the Waters plus the untargetable E all-in beats your immobile kit.

edits.before: Taliyah
edits.after: Fizz

edits.before: First item keeps you ahead as you out-range and roam while he farms melee.
edits.after: First item he holds kill threat on every push — play for tower and roam windows.

edits.before: Taliyah
edits.after: Fizz

edits.before: With two items your poke and roam lead holds, though his assassin scaling keeps it close.
edits.after: With two items his assassin one-shot outpaces your poke — group and wall him off carries.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay nominally yours because you out-poke and out-shove him, but the matchup is execution-heavy: his E untargetable frame dodges your combo, so you must bait it before you commit or you get punished.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 stay nominally yours because you out-poke and out-shove him, but the matchup is execution-heavy: his E untargetable frame dodges your combo, and at 6 the shark flips the lane to his all-in.

edits.before: You stay favoured if you play it clean: Fizz's Chum the Waters shark is his only reliable pick, and you can W yourself out of the shark's path or wall the fish. Keep the wave shoved so his all-in overextends him, and never sit in a straight line for his E-Q gap-close.
edits.after: His spike: the shark plus untargetable E beats you in a straight all-in. Hug tower, keep the wave shoved so his dive overextends him, dodge the fish sideways — never in a straight line for the E-Q gap-close — and save Flash or the wall for the knockup.

edits.before: After items you out-range and out-roam him, but respect that he scales into a squishy-deleting assassin and one landed shark can swing a fight, so wall and W defensively.
edits.after: After items he dictates: an assassin who deletes a squishy off one landed shark. Group, ward your flanks, wall him off the carries, and spend W only to break his dive.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Check it before every step-up. - W Seismic Shove is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1, 8s max. The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo: bait it, then burst the landing. - His shark is 120s at rank 1. - W Seismic Shove is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it.

edits.before: Q from fresh ground on his last-hit, and if he steps to answer, W-shove him across the E-field — the full geometry trade is half a health bar.
edits.after: His Q dash and E hop both cross your minefield if you seed it behind him — W him back through the stones as he lands and the stun is yours.

edits.before: Trading while standing on your own Worked Ground — one-stone Qs lose every exchange your positioning already conceded.
edits.after: Melee is Fizz's world: the Seastone Trident empowered auto is the burst's opening tell — with W down you cannot break the E-Q follow-up.

edits.before: Flash + Teleport or Ignite — TP doubles the roam thesis; Ignite converts the W-E burst into early deletions. Pick by how hard you intend to roam.
edits.after: Flash + Teleport or Ignite — TP extends the roam plan across resets; Ignite converts the W-E burst into early deletions. Pick by how hard you intend to roam.

notes: The two layers disagreed on all 7 chart rows (content: Taliyah 7/7, flagged by the packet against the 45.78% WR; full: Fizz 7/7 against its own tldr admitting Taliyah's early edge). Settled kit-first: Taliyah rows 0-3, Fizz rows 4-6 — every side edit paired with a matching why, and the three flipped content rows carry matching win[]+whys[] edits in the same group. spikes[1].text's false 'W yourself out of the shark's path' (Taliyah W is enemy-displacement only) removed in the rewrite. Suspect name 'Chum the Waters' is the real R name — false positive. Fizz is male.
